12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. paragraphs.text: 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.

8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.

8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Section 7.7 (p0032)**

Section 7.7 requires Customer to pay Vendor "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of annual Fees for *each week* an invoice is unpaid, triggered after only ten days. This fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs/penalties) and the fallback (single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees), and reaches walk-away territory: the weekly accrual can exceed remaining contract value and is triggered by a minor breach.

No other Customer-payable LD, minimum fee, or shortfall charge exists — Sections 9.4 and 10 confirm Customer owes only accrued Fees on termination.

Redline (validated, ok:true): replace 7.7 with customary simple interest at 1%/month on proper undisputed invoices unpaid 30 days past due, plus an express statement that no LD or penalty is payable by Customer — preserving the Section 7.3 dispute-withholding right.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer at 15% of annual Fees for every week an invoice is late, triggered by a mere ten-day payment delay. That fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees), and it sits in walk-away territory because the compounding weekly charge can quickly exceed the remaining contract value and is triggered by a minor breach. No other provision imposes Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum fees, or shortfall charges (Sections 9.4 and 10 confirm Customer owes only accrued Fees on termination). Redline deletes the liquidated damages and substitutes customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving the Section 7.3 withholding right.

Original paragraphs:
p0032: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the Implementation Fee.

Rendered redline:
p0032: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice remains unpaid thirty days after its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at one percent per month (or the highest rate permitted by Applicable Law, if lower) from the due date until payment. No liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer under this Agreement.

Comment:
[Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay is punitive and could exceed the contract value. We have replaced it with customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the dispute-withholding right in Section 7.3.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The MINCOMMIT rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **§ 2.1 (p0013)** — the operative clause: *"No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. **Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement has a dedicated § 11 (Transition Assistance and Data Return) that satisfies the **preferred** position on all material terms:

| Playbook element | Document | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Transition assistance up to 6 months | 11.1 — six months at Customer's request | Met, and priced at rates in the expiring Order Form rather than "then-current rates" — better for us (no uplift exposure) |
| Data return within 30 days, machine-readable | 11.2 — thirty days, complete/commonly used/documented/machine-readable, with relationships and metadata; no withholding for fee disputes | Exceeds preferred |
| Deletion + certification thereafter | 11.3 — secure deletion of active systems and backups as they cycle, officer certification in writing | Met |

Two points worth noting affirmatively rather than as concerns:

- **Deletion sequencing is protective.** 11.3 is triggered only "After Customer confirms successful return," so the walk-away risk (immediate deletion on termination) is foreclosed. The Applicable Law retention carve-out is bounded — the retained copy stays protected and cannot be repurposed.
- **§ 10 does not cut across § 11.** 10.1 ends access only "after any agreed transition period" and preserves our rights in Customer Data; 10.2 adds Deliverable delivery and refunds of prepaid Fees.

One drafting nuance, flagged for awareness only and not a deviation: the 30-day clock in 11.2 runs from *Customer's request* rather than from termination, so we should make the return request promptly at exit. Similarly, 11.1 assistance is request-triggered. Both are consistent with the playbook's "at Customer's request" model language.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 11 meets the preferred position on every material term: (a) 11.1 gives up to six months of transition assistance at Customer's request, at the rates in the expiring Order Form (more favourable to us than "then-current rates"), expressly including knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier and continued service at existing scope and service levels; (b) 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with metadata, and bars withholding over a fee dispute; and (c) 11.3 provides secure deletion with written officer certification. Critically, deletion under 11.3 occurs only "After Customer confirms successful return," so there is no risk of Customer Data being destroyed before we retrieve it, and the legally required retention copy stays protected and use-restricted. Section 10 does not undercut this: 10.1 ends access only after any agreed transition period and preserves our rights in Customer Data, and 10.2 adds Deliverable delivery plus refunds of prepaid Fees. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** Legal (In-House Counsel)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings  
**Party posture:** We represent the Customer.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against nineteen playbook rules. The document is, on the whole, strongly customer-favourable: seventeen of nineteen rules are compliant, several of them above our preferred position. In particular, the IP and deliverables package (§ 14), the perpetual paid-up licence grant (§ 13), Vendor indemnification sitting outside the liability cap (§ 20, § 21.3), unqualified termination for convenience on thirty days' notice (§ 9.4, § 29.4), the six-month transition assistance and data-return regime (§ 11), New York law and venue (§ 28), and the absence of any exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-commitment obligation on us all meet or exceed our preferred positions.

Two issues require negotiation, and both fall into walk-away territory under the playbook:

1. **Liability cap is illusory (§ 21, critical).** The cap is keyed to "Fees," which is defined in §§ 1.5–1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The twelve-month look-back therefore captures no subscription or services charges, leaving a cap far below six months of actual fees. The mutuality, the § 21.2 exclusion of indirect damages and the § 21.3 carve-outs are all acceptable — the defect is the cap basis alone.

2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment (§ 7.7, high).** Liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, fail both our preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). The compounding weekly charge can exceed remaining contract value on a minor breach.

We recommend advancing two targeted redlines and closing on the remainder as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Cap keyed to Fees (one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee per §§ 1.5–1.6); illusory cap, walk-away territory. Carve-outs and mutuality compliant. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week on a ten-day delay; fails preferred and fallback; walk-away territory. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Meets preferred; indemnity is an Excluded Claim under § 21.3, so uncapped (better than fallback super-cap). |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables | Meets preferred in full; Deliverable ownership conditioned on payment and telemetry carve-out noted, both customary. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | Meets preferred; § 24.4 bars Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No exclusivity on us; § 12.4 restraint runs in our favour. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence | Above fallback: Affiliate and contractor use without notice gating; perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination (§ 9.4; § 29.4) | 30 days' notice, accrued Fees only, prepaid Fees refunded; Vendor has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights | Meets preferred on all material terms; no direct system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law and New York County exclusive jurisdiction; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) | Only MFN language runs in our favour; retain as drafted. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope (§ 2.1) | No minimum commitment; reinforced by §§ 7.1, 8.2, 12.3. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No no-hire or no-poach covenant on either Party. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal (§§ 8.2–8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Up to six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; deletion only after confirmed return. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties | Meets preferred; Hosted Services warranted for the subscription term; disclaimer does not swallow express warranties. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | Meets preferred; USD 5M cyber/privacy given Vendor hosts Customer Data. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

Both deviations are identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 21 — Illusory liability cap.** A cap limited to the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee leaves us without meaningful recourse for capped claims. Our position: the cap must be keyed to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor. The existing § 21.2 exclusions and § 21.3 carve-outs remain untouched.

2. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** A compounding weekly charge of 15% of annual Fees, triggered by a ten-day delay, is a penalty we cannot accept. Our position: delete the liquidated damages and substitute customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving our § 7.3 withholding right.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. Issue the two redlines to Vendor: (a) § 21 cap replacement — greater of twelve months of amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000; and (b) § 7.7 deletion with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts substituted.
2. Accompany each redline with a short cover note citing the playbook position and, on the cap, noting that the defect is the definition of "Fees" in §§ 1.5–1.6 rather than the structure of § 21 — this should be an easy fix for Vendor.
3. Confirm with the deal team the expected annual contract value so we can validate that the USD 1,000,000 floor is the right number for this deal.
4. Close on all seventeen compliant items as drafted; no further redlines are required, and we should resist reopening provisions that currently run in our favour (§§ 7.6, 12.4).
5. Escalate to the business sponsor only if Vendor refuses either walk-away item.
"}
